name: Two-Word Social Subtitles
use_when: A short-form edit needs fast, readable subtitles for silent autoplay or noisy environments.
The speaker is moving quickly and long subtitle lines would feel heavy.
Captions may be converted to graphic layers for style, animation, or emphasis.
Premiere auto captions need one-word or very short chunks for a high-energy Reel style.
DaVinci Resolve auto captions need simple styling before a postable reel is exported.
avoid_when: The video is serious testimony or documentary where rapid pop captions would feel inappropriate.
The screen already uses text overlays to show the idea and subtitles would clutter the frame.
The platform or accessibility requirement needs fuller subtitle lines.

timeline_pattern.pattern: transcribe_sequence -> short_chunks -> style_one_caption -> apply_style -> remove_unneeded_captions -> convert_to_graphics_if_animating -> qc
timeline_pattern.chunk_rule: Use one or two words per subtitle for high-energy social style when it improves readability.
timeline_pattern.duration_rule: Keep each short caption onscreen long enough to read; do not exceed about 2 seconds for rapid social chunks unless speech slows.
timeline_pattern.cleanup_rule: Remove captions where visual text already carries the meaning or where captions cover the subject.
timeline_pattern.premiere_one_word_rule: For Premiere one-word social captions, start around 7 characters, 2 seconds max duration, and single-line captions, then manually correct chunks.
timeline_pattern.resolve_simple_rule: For a simple Resolve short, generate captions from audio, limit line length, choose a clean font, and position captions in a safe central/lower area.
timeline_pattern.typography_rule: Chunk by meaning and phrase structure; avoid isolating filler words as the visual emphasis.

motion.rule: Caption animation should be short and should not compete with subject tracking, visual stacks, or transition objects.

sound.rule: Caption timing follows audible speech; fix the mix if music or SFX makes captions do too much work.

captions.rule: Use a consistent style preset, then manually review wording, breaks, emphasis, and placement.

keyframe_values.premiere_one_word_starting_point: Around 7 characters, 2 seconds max duration, single line, and a phone-readable lower-third size.
keyframe_values.max_chunk_duration: About 2 seconds for rapid social subtitles, shorter when speech moves faster.
keyframe_values.line_count: Prefer single-line captions when the visual stack is dense.
keyframe_values.line_breaks: Use phrase-complete line breaks; do not trust automatic wrapping on emphasis captions.

color.rule: Caption fill, stroke, shadow, or backing must remain readable over both bright and dark footage.

implementation.ffmpeg: Generate subtitles from transcript timing, split lines into short chunks, burn after overlays, and inspect phone-size contact sheets for collisions.
implementation.remotion: Represent captions as word chunks with maxWords, maxDurationFrames, styleId, safeRegion, and disabledWhenVisualTextDuplicates fields.
implementation.blender: Use text objects only for custom animated subtitle moments; keep accessibility captions separate when needed.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use auto-captions as a draft, set short chunks, apply style, then delete captions where visual text already explains the moment.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Text > Transcribe Sequence, Create Captions with short line settings, apply an Essential Graphics style, check lower-third placement and size, upgrade to graphics only when animation or styling requires it. In Resolve, use Timeline > AI Tools > Create Subtitles from Audio, set short characters per line, then style the caption track.

common_mistakes: Leaving auto-caption chunks too long for fast short-form pacing.
Leaving Resolve auto captions in the default style without checking font, position, and line length.
Captioning over visual text that already says the same thing.
Converting captions to graphics before timing and wording are correct.
Using rapid pop captions in a serious scene where stable subtitles would be more respectful.
Letting captions cover face, hands, proof, or the transition object.
Applying one-word caption settings without checking whether the phrase becomes too fragmented to understand.
Highlighting filler words because auto-caption chunking isolated them.
qc: Are captions readable at phone size?
Do caption chunks follow the audible speech accurately?
Are one- or two-word chunks used only where they improve pace and readability?
Have unnecessary duplicate captions been removed?
Do captions avoid faces, proof, visual text, and key motion?
Are Resolve auto captions styled and positioned safely before export?
Were Premiere short caption settings reviewed manually instead of trusted as final?
Do line breaks and emphasis follow phrase meaning rather than raw auto-wrap?
